title: Prospectivity Index and signal funnel: prioritized model adoption & fallback hypotheses
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Build a reproducible 'Prospectivity Index' (PI) that ranks public/model-supplier signals by the likelihood they will influence Redwood customers to adopt, substitute, or trigger procurement/rollback actions over a 3-month and 12-month horizon. The PI will power a signal-funnel dashboard, alerting rules for account execs and PMs, and a set of prioritized hypotheses to validate via field probes.

Background & motivation:
- Product teams and commercial orgs increasingly ask for a single surface that translates noisy external model-landscape changes (new releases, performance gains, license changes, pricing moves) into prioritised remediation or opportunity actions.
- Current tracking is manual and siloed; engineering telemetry and procurement signals are not joined with open-model announcements or partner channel intel.

Objectives / Success criteria:
1) Deliver an index score and funnel stage for ~100 tracked model-variants (open-source + key commercial providers) updated daily.
2) Prototype dashboard showing top-20 risers by PI (with reasons) and a changefeed of signals.
3) Define 6 operational alerts (e.g., "High-prospectity supply risk" for customers with >50% usage on at-risk model) and pilot with 3 AE/CS teams.
4) Evaluate PI predictive power: top-10 PI risers should correspond to at least 60% of real procurement inquiries / change requests within 30 days during pilot.

Deliverables:
- Confluence spec: signal taxonomy, scoring formula, and ingestion contract.
- Prototype Looker/Metabase dashboard and CSV export.
- Ingestion ETL mapping + schema for telemetry signals (latency regressions, error rate jumps) and external signals (model release notes, license changes, price cuts).
- Playbook: alerts -> recommended response -> owner mapping.

Signal candidate list (initial):
- Public model release cadence and major bumps (commit messages, release notes)
- Quantization/weight-sharing announcements (affects cost)
- Latency/cost delta measured in our runtime (per-model token cost & p50/p95 latency trends)
- License or export-control changes reported in legal watchlists
- Partner/go-to-market bundling (marketplace listings)
- Field intelligence: inbound procurement, support tickets, AE notes

Hypotheses to test (ranked):
H1: Sudden >20% delta in our per-token cost or p95 latency for a model correlates with a spike in customer migration inquiries within 14 days.
H2: Public release notes referencing proprietary optimizations (e.g., fused kernels) increase adoption probability (PI) among enterprise customers that previously prioritized latency.
H3: License changes (e.g., move to restrictive terms) have high lead-time effect (30–90 days) but strong enterprise impact when triggered.

Trade-offs & constraints:
- Signal freshness vs. noise: high-frequency signals (daily benchmark jitter) need smoothing to avoid alert fatigue.
- Privacy: joining AE notes and customer telemetry requires scoped access controls.
- Label scarcity: supervised approaches will initially rely on heuristic labels from procurement logs; consider semi-supervised scoring.
